A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a simple cycle separator that is much smaller than the previous ones.

we have developed new algorithms that find cycle separators in embedded planar graphs with a number of faces of size at most 2d and the separators have size at most \(\sqrt {2d \cdot v }\)and the running time is O(no(n,n)).
the new upper bounds for the separator problem are the same as the old ones, up to a multiplicative constant, but the new bounds are much better for most graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the norm \(\sqrt { \sum {d_i^2}}\)is a better parameter than \(\sqrt { d \cdot v}\).
the Euclidean norm of the face sizes is the right norm to use in this setting and not the 1-norm.
the Euclidean norm is a more natural measure of the planarity of a graph than the maximum face size.
